thread:
infra-oncall: PROD PAGE — Sapphire Finance (VPC dedicated pool us-west1) p99 latency spike detected, auto-pager triggered @eng-sre, @eng-runtime. Pager details: https://pd.redwood/c/INC-38421 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-38421 created and paged to infra-oncall (priority P1). Summary: p99 > 5s sustained for 8m in sapphire-usw1 dedicated pool.
infra-oncall: Seeing sustained p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 6.2s across several tenants in that pool. No error increase. Need triage — is this queueing at runtime or network?
eng-sre-liz: On it. Joining call now. Can someone drop the specific SLO numbers and customer impact? @support-carlos can you confirm which routes are affected?
support-carlos: Sapphire Finance reports slower confirmations for trade-notify flows since ~09:12 PDT. They see user-facing delays but no 5xx. Our metrics: route /v1/generate?sapphire-account shows p95 1.3s -> 1.9s, p99 6.2s -> 7.1s, throughput unchanged. Token generation rates normal.
prod-obs: Logs show a spike in runtime queue length on nodes in pool sapphire-usw1 between 09:10-09:20. GPU busy %, KV cache hit rate unchanged. Also increased small-batch accumulation (more single-request batches).
eng-runtime-raj: Looking at tail latencies on the runtime: we see one host (sapphire-usw1-node-7) with growing per-req latency and long GC/host-level scheduling stalls. core dump not obvious. Sharing quick top output: 
```
PID   USER  %CPU %MEM   VSZ   RSS TTY  STAT START   TIME COMMAND
12345 root  92.1  3.4  1.2G  350M ?   R    09:11  00:12 /redwood/runtime --pool=sapphire-usw1
```
and dmesg showing few RT throttles.
eng-platform-maya: Node-7 is on older kernel (5.10) while others are 5.15 due to a delayed OOB patch. Rolling kernel restart planned but will cause inflight kill.
infra-oncall: Two parallel mitigations: 1) divert new traffic off sapphire-usw1-node-7 (drain) 2) route a fraction of Sapphire customer traffic to hosted fallback until pool stabilizes. Which is less disruptive?
eng-sre-liz: Drain node now. Command: 
```
redwood infra drain-node --pool sapphire-usw1 --node sapphire-usw1-node-7 --grace 30s
```
I’ll watch for backpressure.
eng-runtime-raj: Draining initiated. Watching batch sizes. Also enabling aggressive batching window to absorb small-batch pressure: 
```
redwood runtime set-config --pool sapphire-usw1 --batching.window_ms 60
```
This should increase batch coalescing but may add a small p95 shift.
support-carlos: I’ll notify customer ops: @customer-ops-jordan can you let Sapphire know we’re diverting traffic and doing node drain, ETA ~10-15m? Keep them on a single update thread.
customer-ops-jordan: Messaging sent to Sapphire (acct-team@sapphire.finance) — told them we expect partial mitigation within 15m, will confirm when all nodes healthy. They asked for timeline for full restore.
account-amelia: Opened enterprise ticket with Sapphire execs, flagged possible SLA credit if >30m degraded. Keeping them in the loop.
eng-platform-maya: After drain, node-7 shows kernel restart started. Reprovisioning with 5.15 and will rejoin. If drain causes queue to spill to other nodes, consider temporary scale-up.
eng-sre-liz: We’re seeing immediate drop in p99 on routes moved off node-7 to other healthy hosts: p99 now ~3.5s. Not fully recovered because we added extra load to remaining nodes.
infra-oncall: Can we spin up an extra replica in the dedicated pool? Is there available quota?
eng-runtime-raj: We can scale pool by +1 replica quickly (hot spare available). Command: 
```
redwood infra scale-pool --pool sapphire-usw1 --replicas +1
```
Scaling now.
prod-obs: New replica provisioned and joined cluster 09:27. Queue depth normalized. p99 down to 2.1s for Sapphire routes, p95 back to ~1.2s. No error rate change.
eng-sre-liz: Good. Keep drain in place until node-7 patched/reimaged. Adding postmortem tag.
infra-oncall: Handoff — I need to go offline for on-call rotation in 10m. Who is taking night shift?
eng-sre-liz: I’ll take runbooks and keep monitoring for 2h, then hand to night oncall. @pagerduty-bot, please update incident owner to eng-sre-liz.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-38421 owner updated to eng-sre-liz.
support-carlos: Customer update: Sent follow-up — "we've drained the problematic node, scaled the pool, and are monitoring. Partial mitigation in place; expected full restore after node reimage." They asked for ETA on reimage.
eng-platform-maya: ETA for reimage + kernel patch and testing ~45m. Will provide exact timeline once kernel tests pass.
eng-sre-liz: For the post-incident checklist: we need: 1) root cause - kernel sched RT throttling on node-7; 2) why node drifted to old kernel (config drift? missing automerge); 3) confirm no tenant data exposure; 4) run capacity recommendations for Sapphire dedicated pool (add hot spare by default). I’ll create postmortem ticket and assign owners.
account-amelia: Prep comms for execs: status, mitigation, ETA. Also double-check SLA exposure.
infra-oncall: Leaving the channel — monitoring alerts still firing but trending down. Thanks everyone.
eng-sre-liz: Leaving only when p99 stable <2s for 15m. Otherwise will escalate to full incident review.
prod-obs: Alerting quieted to info level at 09:45. Will keep dashboard pinned and send 5m summaries.
customer-ops-jordan: Sapphire confirmed improved performance on their end. They will still want a postmortem and timeline.
eng-runtime-raj: Note: we applied temporary batching change. Revert plan: after node reimage and stable 30m, revert batching.window_ms to previous value to avoid increased p95 for other tenants.
eng-sre-liz: Agreed. I’ll schedule revert and document commands in the incident ticket. Closing note: incident severity downgrade to P2 at 09:46 PDT. Postmortem owner: eng-sre-liz.
